report.incident_title: ~8% of order placements failing with connect timeouts to payments
report.summary: Since about 02:05-02:10 UTC, order-svc error rate rose from 0.2-0.3% to about 8%, and order placements fail with connect timeouts to payments-svc. Confirmed by tool results: at 02:05:31 the np-general node-group auto-upgrade drained node ip-10-2-4-11 and evicted two CoreDNS pods; CoreDNS ready replicas fell from 3 to 1 and stayed there through 03:00; CoreDNS p99 lookup latency rose from 2-3 ms to about 4.8-4.9 s; replacement CoreDNS pods were Pending with 'Insufficient cpu'; the failing traces show a dns.lookup span for payments-svc timing out at 2000 ms before the connect timeout; payments-svc latency and error rate stayed flat. The 7.3.1 deploy at 02:00 preceded onset by about 8 minutes, and the 7.3.1 pool-default claim is unverified because the change record has no config diff and no per-version or pool metrics exist. Assumptions, not observed facts: that 6.x pods are unaffected by the DNS slowdown, and that the sampled failures represent all failures. The investigation sample was small (2 traces, 3 logs, no CoreDNS logs). Rolling back 7.3.1 is not supported as a first step, because the failing span is name resolution, though a 7.3.1 contribution cannot be fully excluded without per-version data.
report.root_cause: The np-general managed node-group auto-upgrade (AMI 2026.08.2) drained node ip-10-2-4-11 at 02:05:31, evicting CoreDNS pods coredns-7c9f8-hx2lq and coredns-7c9f8-q8vtd. The replacements could not be scheduled (0/9 nodes available: 9 Insufficient cpu), so CoreDNS ready replicas dropped from 3 to 1 and stayed there. Lookup load on the remaining replica pushed dns_request_latency_p99 to about 4.8 s. order-svc's dns.lookup for payments-svc.prod.svc.cluster.local therefore exceeds the 2000 ms connect timeout, and POST /orders fails with connect_timeout before any TCP connection is attempted on roughly 8% of placements.

hypotheses.statement: Eviction of CoreDNS pods during the np-general node-group auto-upgrade reduced DNS capacity (ready replicas dropped from 3 to 1), causing p99 DNS lookup latency to rise above order-svc’s 2000 ms connect timeout and leading to DNS lookup timeouts on ~8% of order placement requests.

corrective_actions.action: Restore CoreDNS capacity now: free CPU on the remaining nodes or temporarily lower the CoreDNS CPU requests so the two Pending replicas schedule, or scale CoreDNS onto nodes outside np-general as the runbook suggests.
corrective_actions.rationale: The failing stage is DNS resolution, and CoreDNS is down to one ready replica with p99 latency near 4.9 s. Restoring replicas addresses the confirmed cause directly.

corrective_actions.action: Pause or slow the np-general node-group upgrade (it is at 4 of 9 nodes, max unavailable 1) until CoreDNS has a stable replica count spread across nodes.
corrective_actions.rationale: The upgrade is still draining nodes during the incident window, and further drains could evict more CoreDNS pods.

corrective_actions.action: Do not roll back 7.3.1 on the basis of current evidence. Keep it under observation and compare failure rates on 7.3.1 and 6.x pods once per-version metrics are available. Roll back only if DNS latency returns to baseline and errors persist.
corrective_actions.rationale: All observed failures occur at the DNS lookup stage, and the DNS latency change is the only cross-service change that aligns with onset. A rollback would not remove the resolver stall.

corrective_actions.action: Add a PodDisruptionBudget and topology spread constraints for CoreDNS, and reserve enough CPU for its replicas, so node drains cannot take it below a safe replica count.
corrective_actions.rationale: A single node drain removed two of three CoreDNS replicas, and the replacements could not reschedule because capacity was short.

corrective_actions.action: Roll out NodeLocal DNSCache, as planned in the runbook, and consider raising or making configurable the order-svc connect timeout and adding retries for DNS failures.
corrective_actions.rationale: Local caching reduces dependence on the shared CoreDNS replicas, and the current 2000 ms timeout with no retry turns short DNS slowdowns into hard order failures.

corrective_actions.action: Add alerts on CoreDNS ready replicas below the desired count and on CoreDNS p99 lookup latency above about 500 ms, and add a DNS-latency panel to the order-svc dashboard.
corrective_actions.rationale: Replicas fell to 1 and DNS p99 reached 4.9 s, but no CoreDNS or payments-svc alert fired; only OrderErrorRateHigh fired, at 02:12, after failures had begun.

corrective_actions.action: Collect per-version and per-pod order-svc metrics (version label), connection-pool metrics for the OkHttp 5 client, and a 7.3.0 vs 7.3.1 config diff, so the H1 client-pool hypothesis can be tested rather than assumed.
corrective_actions.rationale: The version label query returned no series, and the 7.3.1 pool-default claim has no supporting data, so H1 is currently refuted only by the DNS-stage traces.

incidents.resolution: Rolled back, then re-released with an explicit pool size.

runbooks.title: DNS resolution errors in the cluster
runbooks.body: Symptoms: EAI_AGAIN or DNS timeouts in service logs. Check coredns ready replicas and latency; scale coredns or move it to the system node group. NodeLocal DNSCache is planned but not rolled out.
